text:
alex: Meridian bank POC kickoff scheduled. They want: SSE streaming, function/tool calls with strict JSON schema, and an on-prem agent behind their firewall. Need quick alignment before vendor call.

mira: I can cover security Qs. Main concerns: customer-managed KMS for Private, SOC2 artifacts, and how audit logs are surfaced.

alex: Also pricing: they estimate ~150k tokens/day, 4-week pilot with bursts. Buyer asked if reserved or PAYG is better.

samir: For short pilot, PAYG + burst cap usually wins. Reserved gives lower unit price but requires monthly commit and notice. I'll crunch numbers and post a 4-week estimate.

jordan: SDK note: recommend sdk-node v1.2+ or sdk-python v0.9+ for streaming helpers. Example node snippet: 
```js
const client = new RedwoodClient({ token: EPHEMERAL });
for await (const chunk of client.stream({ model: 'redwood-stream-1' })) {
  processChunk(chunk);
}
```
We'll provide this in the repo.

amanda: (typo correction) -> mira: also need nginx sample for on-prem ingress: TLS termination + mTLS to agent. I'll add an nginx.conf snippet to the runbook.

samir: Ephemeral creds are supported via short-lived tokens (default TTL 5m). SSE connect example: 
```bash
EPHEM=$(curl -s "+https://auth.redwood.ai/v1/ephemeral?role=stream" -H "Authorization: Basic $CLIENT_SECRET")
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer $EPHEM" \
  "https://private.redwood.local/streams?model=redwood-stream-1&inst=meridian"
```
Add header `X-Tenant` for routing.

mira: For structured toolcalls they want a schema named `meridian_txn_v1` with tx_id, amount_cents, merchant_id, decision, confidence_score. Will attach JSON Schema file. Sample system prompt: 
```
System: Output ONLY JSON matching meridian_txn_v1 (no prose)
User: Analyze and return transaction object for: \"Charge $12.34 at Merchant 123\"
```
We should show validation step after model response.

jordan: Also customer asked about fallback behavior: prefer on-prem agent but failover to hosted Redwood if on-prem capacity low. Smart routing supports region->fallback chains but document latency and data residency tradeoffs.

alex: Good. Can we offer a short test harness so they can run a synthetic traffic generator against the on-prem agent and see CPU/GPU usage?

samir: Yes, we have a load-test script (`tools/loadgen.py`) that can be parameterized. I'll prepare a quick runbook: how to run with ephemeral creds, expected QPS, and how to interpret KV cache warmup effects.

mira: Security deliverables I will assemble: SOC2 redacted PDF, KM S integration doc (Customer-Managed KMS for Private), per-tenant audit log screenshots, and the completed security questionnaire answers.

alex: Action items: Samir -> cost comparison + loadgen + ephemeral how-to by EOD. Jordan -> SDK snippets + nginx ingress notes + schema validation example. Mira -> security artifacts and questionnaire answers. I'll schedule the kickoff and include infra/infosec.

presales-bot: Created Jira POC-2154: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/POC-2154 and added checklist items for SDK snippets, security pack, cost estimate.

alex: I'll run the call. Please drop links to snippets into the Jira ticket when ready. :thumbsup:

mira: One more: they want an example of chunked function-call where model emits `commands[]` then the agent invokes them in order with idempotency keys. We'll demo with a small transactions processing flow.

samir: Noted. I'll include an example with idempotency header and retry semantics.

jordan: I'll push a minimal example repo branch and paste link into the ticket.

alex: Thanks team — meeting invite sent for 10:30 PT.
